Report Description/// NOAA/NESDIS MPSR ISSUED FOR: GULF OF AMERICA /// POSSIBLE, UNCONFIRMED OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. REPORT DATE: 08-23-2026 REPORT TIME: 2330 UTC REGION: GULF OF AMERICA SUB REGION: N/A AREA/BLOCK: EUGENE ISLAND 316 IMAGE DATE: 08-23-2026 IMAGE TIME: 1638 UTC DATA SOURCE: LANDSAT8 MODE: MULTISPECTRAL RESOLUTION: 30 METER LOCATION: 28°15'45" N/91°37'06" W AREA: 6.24 SQUARE KILOMETERS CONFIDENCE: HIGH REPORT MAP/GIS FILES: HTTPS://WWW.OSPO.NOAA.GOV/PRODUCTS/OCEAN/MARINEPOLLUTION/ REMARKS: POSSIBLE OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. THIS ANOMALY IS UNCONFIRMED AS OIL. A LINEAR SLICK APPEARED TO EMANATE FROM A PIPELINE LOCATED IN THE EUGENE ISLAND BLOCK 316 AREA, APPROXIMATELY 84 NM SSE OF MARSH ISLAND, LOUISIANA. THIS ANOMALY IS BELIEVED TO BE ASSOCIATED WITH NOAA NESDIS RESPONSE LINK NRC REPORTS TO INCLUDE #1471024 ON 8/17 AND OTHER RECENT OBSERVATIONS. THE SLICK'S OUTER EDGES APPEARED DARK-TONED, AND THE INNER PORTIONS INCLUDED A SILVER AND WHITE SHIMMERY HUE THAT INDICATED POSSIBLE THICKER OIL. ALSO, THE ANOMALY DID NOT TEST POSITIVE FOR VEGETATION, INCLUDED SHARP EDGES AND APPEARED OUT OF PLACE. IT MEASURED APPROXIMATELY 14.3 NM IN LENGTH, AND 0.4 NM AT THE WIDEST POINT. WINDS NEAR THE TIME OF THE IMAGE WERE OUT OF THE WNW AT 5 KTS, WHICH ALIGNED WITH THE TRAJECTORY OF THE LINEAR ANOMALY. UNCERTAINTIES: THE FULL EXTENT OF THE SLICK MAY HAVE BEEN UNDERESTIMATED DUE TO CLOUD COVER AND OTHER FALSE POSITIVES THAT MAY HAVE OBSCURED SECTIONS OF THE ANOMALY. IF YOU WOULD LIKE TO SHARE ANY FEEDBACK ABOUT THIS REPORT OR HAVE QUESTIONS, PLEASE CONTACT THE OPERATIONAL ANALYST AT (301) 683-1403 OR SEND TO OCEANMAP@NOAA.GOV. THIS ANOMALY IS BELIEVED TO BE ASSOCIATED WITH NOAA NESDIS RESPONSE LINK NRC REPORTS TO INCLUDE #1471024 ON 8/17 AND OTHER RECENT OBSERVATIONS. THE SLICK'S OUTER EDGES APPEARED DARK-TONED, AND THE INNER PORTIONS INCLUDED A SILVER AND WHITE SHIMMERY HUE THAT INDICATED POSSIBLE THICKER OIL. ALSO, THE ANOMALY DID NOT TEST POSITIVE FOR VEGETATION, INCLUDED SHARP EDGES AND APPEARED OUT OF PLACE. IT MEASURED APPROXIMATELY 14.3 NM IN LENGTH, AND 0.4 NM AT THE WIDEST POINT. WINDS NEAR THE TIME OF THE IMAGE WERE OUT OF THE WNW AT 5 KTS, WHICH ALIGNED WITH THE TRAJECTORY OF THE LINEAR ANOMALY. UNCERTAINTIES: THE FULL EXTENT OF THE SLICK MAY HAVE BEEN UNDERESTIMATED DUE TO CLOUD COVER AND OTHER FALSE POSITIVES THAT MAY HAVE OBSCURED SECTIONS OF THE ANOMALY.
